newsitem.title: USA: AT&T completes undersea fiber optic network.
newsitem.headline: AT&T completes undersea fiber optic network.

text.p: AT&T said on Tuesday it has activated the northern segment of TPC-5, concluding construction of its transpacific undersea fiber optic network to connect the United States and Asia.

TPC-5 links Guam, Hawaii, Japan and the United States mainland. The newly completed northern segment connects the Bandon cable station to landing points at Miyazaki, Japan, and San Luis Obispo, California, the company said.
The southern route, in service since 1995, continues from San Luis Obispo to landing points at Keawaula, Hawaii, Tumon Bay, Guam, and Miyazaki and Ninomiya, Japan.
The 22,560-kilometer TPC-5 has the ability to transmit five gigabits per second over one fiber pair, capacity equal to 320,000 simultaneous phone calls.

The company said the network is also considered to be the first undersea fiber cable network in the Pacific to feature a closed loop rather than a point-to-point system which gives it added restoration capabilities. If there is a network disruption, the company said service can be restored by shifting voice, data and video signals to the spare fiber on the network.

"TPC-5's high capacity, self-healing capabilities and the added route diversity offer customers the greatest reliability for communications across the Pacific," said William Carter, president of AT&T's Submarine Systems Inc.
